Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: RIGHT knee pain
Comparison: Right knee x-ray [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Marginal osteophytes are noted at the patella, distal femur, proximal tibia, and intercondylar eminence. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Focal high-grade chondral loss involving the anterior weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle with subchondral cystic changes.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade chondral loss involving the median ridge, medial and lateral patellar facets with subchondral cystic changes and reactive edema. Diffuse high-grade chondral loss primarily involving the lateral and central trochlea with subchondral cystic changes and reactive edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Degenerative type signal in the MCL without tear. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritis primarily affecting the patellofemoral compartment.
2.	Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation.
3.	If patient pain persists, geniculate nerve ablation can be considered.

ΤΕΧΝΙΚΗ: Η εξέταση έγινε µε ακολουθίες παλµών Τ1, PD fs και Τ2 βαθµιδωτής ηχούς. ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ: - Εκτεταµένες οστεοαρθριτικές αλλοιώσεις εντοπιζόµενες ιδίως στο έσω µεσάρθριο διάστηµα µε ολικού πάχους απώλεια αρθρικού χόνδρου της κνήµης και του µηριαίου, εκφύλιση και υπεξάρθρηµα του έσω µηνίσκου καθώς και εκφύλιση του έξω µηνίσκου, παρουσία επιχείλιων οστεοφύτων και παρουσία υπαρθρικών κυστικών αλλοιώσεων ιδίως στην περιοχή των µεσοκονδυλίων επαρµάτων της κνήµης. - Οστεοχόνδρινο ξένο σωµα αναγνωρίζεται εντός της µεσοκονδύλιας εντοµής επί τα εκτός και οπισθίως του προσθίου χιαστού συνδέσµου στο πλαίσιο δευτεροπαθούς συνοβιακής οστεοχονδρωµάτωσης. - Στο πλαίσιο των προαναφερθέντων εκφυλιστικών αλλοιώσεων αναγνωρίζεται επίσης εκτεταµένο υπαρθρικό οστεοµυελικό οίδηµα στον έσω µηριαίο και κνηµιαίο κόνδυλο, η έκταση του οποίου θέτει την υπόνοια συνύπαρξης καταγµάτων ανεπάρκειας (subchondral insufficiency fractures - γνωστών και ως SONK). Σκόπιµη κρίνεται η αποφόρτιση του γόνατος και ο επανέλεγχος µε την πάροδο 6 εβδοµάδων. - Ανωµαλία παρυφής του χόνδρου της επιγονατίδας ως επι αρχόµενων αλλοιώσεων (ICRS grade 1-2). - Χωρίς αξιόλογα ευρήµατα από τον έλεγχο του λοιπού οστικού µυελού, των χιαστών και των πλαγίων συνδέσµων.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion. No Bakers cyst. Small ganglion cyst associated with the medial head gastrocnemius insertion.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Degenerative multidirectional tear, with longitudinal horizontal tear at the junction of the body and posterior horn, and radial tear of the posterior horn. There is mild meniscal extrusion. Full-thickness chondral loss at the medial femoral condyle, with diffuse high-grade medial articular cartilage thinning. Small marginal osteophytes in keeping with mild medial compartment osteoarthrosis.
Thickening of the MCL with mild overlying edema in keeping with grade 1 injury.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Blunting of the inner free edge of the body of the lateral meniscus in keeping with a small partial radial tear, on a background of degenerative signal changes. Mild partial-thickness chondral thinning of lateral articular cartilage.
Normal lateral collateral ligament structures. Trace of fluid within the popliteal recess.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Mucoid degeneration of the ACL, with early ganglion cyst formation within the distal insertion. Normal PCL.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Normal extensor mechanism. Normal fat pads.
Full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial patellar articular facet with mild subchondral reactive edema.
Small marginal osteophytes in keeping with mild osteoarthrosis.

Bones:
Normal.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.Tricompartmental osteoarthrosis/chondropathy as detailed above.
2.Degenerative multidirectional medial meniscal tear with mild meniscal extrusion.
3.Small lateral meniscal partial radial tear.

MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS


> Increased interstitial signal of distal quadriceps tendon on F/S T2WI and incrased fat stranding over anterior suprapatellar fat pad, R/O grade 1 injury and suprapatellar fat pad inflammation.
> Suspicious of mild increased singal intensity of patellar articular cartialge on F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 chondromalacia.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to contusion or peripheral vascularity.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> No evidence of bone contusion is noted.
> Minimal joint effusion and suprapatellar plica.

Impression: 
1. Grade 1 injury of distal quadriceps tendon and anterior suprapatellar fat pad inflammation.
2. R/O grade 1 patellar chondromalacia.
3. No strong evidence of full thickness tear of ACL.
4. R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to contusion or peripheral vascularity.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

MRI of left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS




> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> No strong MR evidence of tear of lateral meniscus.
> The contour of ACL and MCL in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury.
> The contour of PCL within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Fluid accumulation along proximal LCL and popliteus tendon with mild increased singal of the tendon/ ligament on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury and mild bursitis.
> Bone marrow edema in medial tibial tuberosity, more prominent at subchondral region.
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, with internal septums and mild perifocal edema, in favor of Baker's cyst, more than 7 cm in length.
> Increased fat stranding along the pes anserinus, R/O paratendinitis.
> Mild irregular contour of articular surface of patella, in favor of grade 2 chondromalacia.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with medial/ lateral plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Mild subcutaneous edema over anterior aspect of knee.
 
Impression: 
1. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
2. Grade 1 injury of ACL and MCL.
   Grade 1 injury of proximal popliteus tendon and LCL with adjacent bursitis(Srs/Img: [ID]/21)
3. Mild synovitis of left knee and prominent Baker's cyst with mild perifocal edema; patellar plicae.
4. Mild paratendinitis of pes anserinus; mild bursitis abutting proximal LCL.
5. Grade 2 chondromalacia of patella and medial femorotibial joint.
6. Bone marrow edmea over medial tibial plateua.
